key_insight: The paper co-designs algorithm, code, and hardware so high-rate self-dual bicycle codes can support parallel STAR magic-state injections for fault-tolerant lattice simulation with much lower qubit overhead.
engineering_relevance: It gives a concrete path to practical early fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom hardware by reducing both encoding cost and Clifford overhead while preserving fast execution.
method: Use translation symmetries of the target lattice to select tunable bicycle chain codes.
Exploit disjoint logical representatives to inject STAR states in parallel across all logical qubits in a block.
Compile logical operations into low-depth acousto-optic-deflector shifts on neutral-atom platforms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports end-to-end estimates such as 2240 physical qubits and about 200 s per shot for an 8×8 transverse-field Ising simulation, with roughly 5.5× less space than a surface-code STAR baseline at similar speed.
watch_item: Resource estimates depend on practical post-selection rates, hardware error rates, and successful implementation of the symmetry-based compilation on real neutral-atom systems.
paper_title: Fast and Parallel High-Rate STAR Architecture for Megaquop Quantum Simulation
